title: Challenge: SSH dynamic (SOCKS) proxy
intro: Instead of forwarding a single port, you want a general-purpose proxy that routes arbitrary traffic through a remote host, as if you were on its network. That's an SSH dynamic forward: a local SOCKS proxy.

steps.instruction: Start a SOCKS proxy on local port 1080 through jump.example.com, without a remote shell.
steps.success: SOCKS5 proxy listening on 127.0.0.1:1080 via jump.example.com.
steps.fail: Use ssh -D LOCAL_PORT to user@jump.example.com (add -N for no shell).

steps.instruction: Make a request through the proxy: curl an internal site using the SOCKS5 proxy on port 1080.
steps.success: Reached intranet.corp through jump.example.com, your traffic exited from the remote network.
steps.fail: Point curl at the SOCKS proxy, e.g. with --socks5 localhost:1080.

done: Solved! `ssh -D` gives you a SOCKS proxy, one tunnel for any destination. Browsers and most tools can use it directly.
